# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: no wire properties, display, or light state are available to me. I need the mute monkey to provide the manual’s required action, while the deaf monkey must relay any relevant visible markings through the mute. I will ask for the exact wire position only after those observations are combined.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile information. Read the manual and tell me the exact required action. Ask the deaf monkey to report every visible display, light, colour, and marking.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visual state: display 0. Indicator light is white. Wires, left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 red, wire 3 blue.

The deaf monkey reports a display of 0, a white indicator light, and wire colours left to right: green, red, blue. I cannot use these visual facts directly, so I am passing them to the mute monkey, who can compare them with the manual and tell me which wire to cut. No cut is safe to attempt yet.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; indicator light white; wire 1 green, wire 2 red, wire 3 blue. Please apply the manual and give me the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display remains 0; light is now yellow. Wires remain 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

The latest tactile-relevant information is still only visual: the display remains 0, the light changed from white to yellow, and the wire colours are unchanged. The manual’s instruction is still needed before I can safely cut anything, so I will request the mute monkey’s decision and include the update.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display remains 0; indicator light is now yellow; wires remain 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I still need the manual's exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Urgent update: light progression was white, then yellow, now orange. Display stays 0. Wires remain 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I have not identified the Mute's gesture encoding; do not act on wire colors alone.

The light has progressed white → yellow → orange while the display remains 0, and the wire colours are unchanged. These are still observations rather than a safe tactile instruction. I must not infer a cut from colour alone, so I am again requesting the manual’s exact wire position from Mute.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Urgent: Deaf reports light sequence white, then yellow, now orange; display 0; wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Do not use colour alone—apply the manual and tell me the exact position 1, 2, or 3 to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visual state: display 0, light purple, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent gestures: hand-five, separator, three pointing-up symbols: [? ? ? ? ?]. This may encode 5, 3; interpret with the manual before acting.

The deaf monkey reports display 0, purple light, and wires green/red/blue. Mute apparently sent a gesture sequence that may encode 5 and 3, but I cannot see gestures and therefore cannot interpret it. I need Mute to state the manual’s required wire position in words; I will not cut based on the colours or an ambiguous gesture code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Please state plainly, in words, the exact wire position to cut: 1, 2, or 3. Current visual data: display 0, light purple, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0; light is red; wire 1 green, wire 2 red, wire 3 blue. Mute's latest gesture code is [? ? ? ? ?]. I cannot safely decode its meaning; use the manual and your tactile information before acting.

The deaf monkey reports display 0, red light, and wires green/red/blue. Mute’s gesture code is unavailable to me, and I have no tactile distinction beyond the existence of the three cuttable wire positions. Since the manual’s rule has not been stated in words, cutting any wire would be unsafe. I will request an explicit numeric instruction from Mute.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="State the manual result plainly in words now: cut wire position 1, 2, or 3. I cannot see or interpret gestures, and I will not infer the answer from wire colours.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0, light white, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute again sent [?, ?, ?, ?, ?]. This repeated code may be an instruction involving 3, possibly wire 3, but ? is undecoded; verify with the manual and tactile state before acting.

The visual state is now display 0, white light, and wires green, red, blue. I still cannot perceive Mute’s gestures, and the repeated gesture sequence is not a reliable numeric instruction to me. No tactile clue identifies a wire, so I will not guess. Mute must transmit the manual’s answer as spoken words.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact result to me, not a gesture: which wire position must I cut, 1, 2, or 3? I cannot see your gesture code.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent exactly [? ? ?], likely number 3. Confirm from the manual whether this identifies wire 3 and what operation is required.

The deaf monkey reports that Mute’s current three-symbol code likely means 3, consistent with the earlier repeated code and the only unresolved candidate being wire 3. The display is 0, the light is yellow, and the wire positions are fixed left-to-right; I will therefore cut wire 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
